title: Migrate relational queries to v1
description: Compare relational queries on Drizzle ORM 0.45.4 and 1.0.0-rc.5, side by side.

steps.label: Relations
steps.title: Relations in one place
steps.body:
This guide compares Drizzle ORM **0.45.4** with **1.0.0-rc.5**. In 0.45.4, each table gets its own `relations()` call. In 1.0.0-rc.5, `defineRelations` groups the relations in one declaration.

The query on each side loads the same authors, posts and comments. Press **Run** to compare them. If you are learning relations for the first time, start with [Drizzle in five minutes](/examples/drizzle-in-five-minutes).

meta.summary: Two ways to declare the same relations.
meta.changed: Both sides returned the same authors, posts, and comments.

steps.label: Filters
steps.title: Filters become objects
steps.body:
In 0.45, `where` takes a callback with operators. In 1.0 it takes a plain object keyed by column.

Same query, same rows. Only the filter syntax differs.

meta.summary: Filter by name on both sides.

steps.label: Nested
steps.title: Nested with, limit, orderBy
steps.body:
`with` nests the same way on both releases. `orderBy` is a callback in 0.45 and an object in 1.0; `limit` works the same.

The name filter still selects Ada. Inside her posts, descending ID order and `limit: 1` keep only the post with the highest ID. This limits her posts, not the number of users.

replace.with:
where: (users, { like }) => like(users.name, "A%"),
  with: { posts: { columns: { title: true }, orderBy: (posts, { desc }) => [desc(posts.id)], limit: 1 } },

where: { name: { like: "A%" } },
  with: { posts: { columns: { title: true }, orderBy: { id: "desc" }, limit: 1 } },

meta.summary: Load Ada with just her highest-ID post.
meta.changed: Both sides returned Ada with one post: Relations in one query.

steps.label: Columns
steps.title: Partial columns
steps.body: `columns` reads the same on both releases: `true` picks a column, `false` leaves it out and keeps the rest.

meta.summary: Leave out a column instead of picking one.
meta.changed: Both sides omitted `id` and returned the other columns.
